title: Unified Logistics Schema Integration
business: A global logistics provider managing diverse shipping, warehousing, and customs data across disparate legacy microservices.
problem: The engineering team struggles with over-fetching and under-fetching data because existing REST endpoints return rigid, bloated payloads that require multiple sequential network requests to assemble a single shipment view.
solution: Implementing a GraphQL layer allows the frontend to request exactly the fields needed for a shipment dashboard in a single round trip, using a strongly typed schema to map relationships between disparate services.
steps: Define a unified schema using GraphQL types to represent core entities like Shipments, Warehouses, and CustomsDocs.
Implement resolvers that fetch data from underlying legacy REST APIs and aggregate the results.
Expose a single HTTP endpoint that validates incoming queries against the schema before execution.
Enable introspection to allow frontend developers to discover available fields and relationships dynamically.
outcome: Developers achieve higher frontend velocity by reducing the number of network requests and eliminating the need for client-side data transformation logic.
limitation: The primary trade-off is the complexity of the N+1 problem, where a single query for a list of shipments could trigger excessive backend requests; this is checked by monitoring resolver execution patterns and implementing data loaders.
